I upvoat (upgoat?) anything I'm happy to see. This can be OC, unoriginal content, satire, etc. I go with the flow of my emotions.

My rules for voating are as follows.

  1. If I think more people should see this, upvoat.

  2. If I think fewer people should see this, downvoat.

  3. If I don't care enough to form an opinion on whether a given contribution should spread, cast no voat.

  4. If I don't want to see posts from the sub on /v/all or /v/all/new, block it.

  5. If I feel a conversation could benefit from my contribution, post.

It acts as a massive community magnet. By allowing people the space to learn any issue they desire it eliminates the issue of poor coordination between voaters who otherwise might be fascinated by an issue of interest, be it say government nasties, major stories of the week and long-term social concerns.

More importantly it presents those issues in a way that is more democratic than a news site. This is the most important function of /r/outoftheloop. It stops MSM editorialization from buttfucking stories to fit their agenda and so weakens the ability for interest groups to force false narratives.

Last but not least by its very nature an out of the loop sub encourages voaters to help each other. Out of the loop has confrontation, but it is less brutal than say a 'politics' sub because the focus is on consensus, not infighting masquerading as debate. That helps to reduce tension that might be suppressed elsewhere because of the eternally combative mood.
More than any other subverse, voat needs /v/outoftheloop to be stronger
